performance.scope: Six fresh processes per runtime and all source-load permutations. Twelve balanced common >=20ms batches per workflow, same-source duplicate, pre-timing numerical/alias/caller-state checks. Thirty existing public0.72API workflows,including10functionalJVP flows using the same public APIs on both sides. No composed baseline. No nativeTorch/GPU/cold-start/universal speedup claim.

findings: All18fresh30flow latency children passed exact-source,program,numerical,dtype/shape,alias and caller-state checks. Both sides use the same public APIs.

Other20API B/A medians0.9924–1.0109 and B/duplicate0.9910–1.0075;A/A0.9942–1.0164. No material persistent latency regression requiring added controls was identified within this experiment;not universal no-regression evidence.

23/30JVP runtime-workflow medians improve by over1% against both denominators. Most targeted cases improve about1–3%;Parameter cases are practically unchanged and CPU normalization gains are small. No universal speedup claim.

Initial one-process allocation observations had1.9%A/A variation in a single-Tensor case. Additional6fresh source-load/case/call-order controls retain those original samples and show JVP B/A/Bduplicate tracked peaks0.9631–0.9920 with A/A1.0000medians.

The same controls show existing HVP peak increases0.24%,0.85%,1.25% on three small fixtures. These costs are retained,not classified as memory improvement or assigned an isolated cause. Not RSS,WASM/GPU memory or latency evidence.

Scoped JVP duration/temporary-allocation gains plus preserved subclass dispatch and expanded regression coverage justify proceeding to full application validation,with the modest gains and HVP peak costs disclosed.
